text: Four models now exist with no tests: the orders and payments staging models, the intermediate join, and fct_orders. Each gets the tests that match what could actually go wrong with it.

fct_orders is grain one-row-per-order. not_null on order_id catches a broken join dropping the key. Unique catches the thing this project's design specifically tries to avoid: a join producing more than one row per order. Keep that one in mind.

A relationships test on customer_id checks referential integrity: every customer_id value in fct_orders has to actually exist in the customers mart — the same mart this chapter's intermediate model already joins against.

Status gets accepted_values, using the exact real status list you recorded from raw_orders back in Lesson 1 — placed, shipped, completed, returned. That catches a typo or an undocumented new status before it reaches Ops's report.
Next lesson: generating and reading dbt docs — dbt docs generate, dbt docs serve, and the real lineage graph these new models now sit inside.
